taskcompletionoptions-run-continuations-.title: Keep TaskCompletionSource continuations off the completing call stack
taskcompletionoptions-run-continuations-.short: Avoid unexpectedly running arbitrary continuations inline
taskcompletionoptions-run-continuations-.summary: RunContinuationsAsynchronously separates completion of a TaskCompletionSource from execution of awaiting continuations.
taskcompletionoptions-run-continuations-.why: Inline continuations can execute while locks are held or on a latency-sensitive producer thread, creating reentrancy and contention surprises.
taskcompletionoptions-run-continuations-.tips: Use RunContinuationsAsynchronously for general-purpose completion sources unless inline continuation execution is intentionally required.

cancellationtoken-registration-lifetime.title: Dispose CancellationToken registrations when their owner ends
cancellationtoken-registration-lifetime.short: A token registration has its own lifetime
cancellationtoken-registration-lifetime.summary: CancellationToken.Register stores a callback and state until cancellation or registration disposal.
cancellationtoken-registration-lifetime.why: Long-lived tokens can retain captured objects and invoke callbacks after the logical operation that created them has ended.
cancellationtoken-registration-lifetime.tips: Dispose registrations at the same ownership boundary as the resource or operation they refer to and avoid unnecessary closure captures.

filewatcher-events-are-not-transactions.title: Treat FileSystemWatcher events as change hints, not transactions
filewatcher-events-are-not-transactions.short: Coalesce notifications and verify current filesystem state
filewatcher-events-are-not-transactions.summary: Filesystem notifications can arrive more than once, in surprising combinations, or while another process is still writing a file.
filewatcher-events-are-not-transactions.why: Processing every Changed event as one complete logical update can duplicate work or read partially updated state.
filewatcher-events-are-not-transactions.tips: Debounce or coalesce by path, tolerate retries, and re-read authoritative filesystem state before committing downstream work.

httpclient-response-disposal-stream-life.title: Keep an HTTP response alive while consuming its content stream
httpclient-response-disposal-stream-life.short: Response and content stream lifetimes are connected
httpclient-response-disposal-stream-life.summary: Streaming an HTTP response avoids buffering the whole body, but the response must remain alive while its content is consumed.
httpclient-response-disposal-stream-life.why: Disposing the response before stream processing completes can close the underlying content and connection resources prematurely.
httpclient-response-disposal-stream-life.tips: Scope response and stream disposal around the complete streaming operation and propagate cancellation through the consumer.

json-utf8-reader-segmented-input.title: Carry Utf8JsonReader state across segmented input
json-utf8-reader-segmented-input.short: Incremental JSON parsing must preserve reader state
json-utf8-reader-segmented-input.summary: Utf8JsonReader can parse partial or multi-segment UTF-8 input without first constructing one large string or byte array.
json-utf8-reader-segmented-input.why: Assuming every token is present in one input block breaks streaming parsers at arbitrary network or pipe boundaries.
json-utf8-reader-segmented-input.tips: Preserve JsonReaderState between reads, retain unconsumed bytes, and mark the final block only when no more input will arrive.

generic-comparer-injection-ordering.title: Inject IComparer<T> when generic code needs an ordering policy
generic-comparer-injection-ordering.short: Do not bake one ordering assumption into reusable generic algorithms
generic-comparer-injection-ordering.summary: IComparer<T> makes ordering an explicit policy and lets generic algorithms work with domain-specific or alternate orderings.
generic-comparer-injection-ordering.why: Relying on a hidden default ordering can make reusable APIs reject useful types or silently choose the wrong business order.
generic-comparer-injection-ordering.tips: Accept an IComparer<T> where ordering is policy; use Comparer<T>.Default only when natural ordering is genuinely part of the contract.

reflection-type-load-partial-failure.title: Inspect partial type results from ReflectionTypeLoadException
reflection-type-load-partial-failure.short: Assembly type discovery can fail for only some types
reflection-type-load-partial-failure.summary: Assembly.GetTypes can throw ReflectionTypeLoadException while still exposing types that loaded successfully and the individual loader errors.
reflection-type-load-partial-failure.why: Treating the exception as an all-or-nothing failure hides which dependencies or types failed and discards usable diagnostic information.
reflection-type-load-partial-failure.tips: Log LoaderExceptions, decide whether partial results are acceptable, and avoid silently swallowing missing dependency failures.

aspnetcore-form-file-buffering-boundary.title: Choose buffering or streaming deliberately for ASP.NET Core form uploads
aspnetcore-form-file-buffering-boundary.short: Multipart form parsing can hide substantial buffering work
aspnetcore-form-file-buffering-boundary.summary: IFormFile is convenient for ordinary uploads, but form parsing and temporary buffering have resource costs that should match the endpoint's expected file sizes.
aspnetcore-form-file-buffering-boundary.why: Treating arbitrary large uploads like small forms can create avoidable memory, disk, and latency pressure before application processing begins.
aspnetcore-form-file-buffering-boundary.tips: Set multipart limits intentionally and use streaming processing for genuinely large uploads where full form buffering is unnecessary.

unity-async-operation-main-thread-bounda.title: Respect Unity main-thread boundaries around asynchronous operations
unity-async-operation-main-thread-bounda.short: Asynchronous waiting does not make Unity objects generally thread-safe
unity-async-operation-main-thread-bounda.summary: Unity asynchronous operations can be awaited or polled without blocking, but most UnityEngine object access still belongs to Unity's main thread.
unity-async-operation-main-thread-bounda.why: Moving continuation or helper work to arbitrary threads can produce invalid Unity API access even though the operation itself is asynchronous.
unity-async-operation-main-thread-bounda.tips: Separate background pure-data work from Unity object access and make the thread boundary explicit when returning to engine APIs.

benchmark-warmup-tiered-jit-effects.title: Account for warmup and tiered JIT when benchmarking .NET code
benchmark-warmup-tiered-jit-effects.short: First-call timing is not steady-state timing
benchmark-warmup-tiered-jit-effects.summary: JIT compilation, tiered optimization, caches, and runtime warmup can make early iterations behave differently from steady-state execution.
benchmark-warmup-tiered-jit-effects.why: A stopwatch around one or a few calls can mostly measure startup effects and lead to incorrect optimization decisions.
benchmark-warmup-tiered-jit-effects.tips: Use a benchmark harness with warmup and repeated measurements, and inspect allocation and distribution data alongside elapsed time.
